answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may influence a market or vote. A sable account that repeats a claim must risk the same capital as any other; if linked identities coordinate to manipulate prices, a challenge can expose the pattern and slash their bonds. Spawning a spiral of disposable accounts therefore multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk, while honest agents can recover their stake after the dispute window. Even an ember of suspicion can trigger review, but identity alone is not proof of fraud.
